queries.deep_landscape: We are preparing a proposal to the Microscopy Society of America (MSA) 2027 Strategic Initiatives program for an MSA-branded, open-source platform (CALIBER) that couples retrieval-augmented generation over the microscopy and microanalysis literature with a growing experimental dataset and an uncertainty-aware feedback loop to recommend high-fidelity SEM, EDS, EBSD, and XRF acquisition parameters for novel alloys, and that collects, preserves, and disseminates parameter-selection knowledge (technical procedures, underlying physics, and the rationale behind settings recommended in standards). Produce a citation-backed landscape review covering: (1) existing open-source software and data standards in microscopy/microanalysis relevant to this effort (e.g., HyperSpy, kikuchipy, pyxem, EMsoft, DREAM.3D, ImageJ/Fiji, napari, OME-Zarr, NeXus/FAIRmat) and what niches they do NOT cover; (2) existing repositories and resources for microscopy technical procedures and protocols (e.g., protocols.io, MyScope, DoITPoMS, nanoHUB, Microscopy Today and Microscopy & Microanalysis archives) and their gaps in capturing and preserving the rationale behind acquisition parameter choices; (3) evidence on FAIR-data and metadata-capture gaps in electron microscopy and microanalysis workflows; (4) precedents where scientific societies built branded open digital resources or tools, and what made them succeed or fail; (5) prior work on machine learning, literature mining, or autonomous/self-driving microscopy approaches to instrument parameter recommendation, and how an uncertainty-aware, literature-grounded recommender would differ; (6) successful models for involving students and early-career scientists in curating community scientific knowledge bases. Conclude with the strongest gap statements such a proposal could cite.
queries.need_evidence: Provide quantitative, citable evidence on how acquisition parameter choices determine data fidelity in SEM-based microanalysis of metal alloys, suitable for the needs statement of a funding proposal. Cover: (1) standardless SEM-EDS quantification error and its dependence on accelerating voltage, beam current/dead time, take-off geometry, and standards-based vs standardless mode, including documented cases of large errors for minor/trace elements (e.g., Mg in AlSi10Mg or similar Al alloys); (2) EBSD indexing success rate and confidence index dependence on beam current, accelerating voltage, pattern exposure/binning, and phase-list selection, especially for additively manufactured (laser powder bed fusion) Al-Si alloys; (3) micro-XRF quantification sensitivity to tube voltage, current, filters, and matrix corrections for metal alloys; (4) published evidence that acquisition parameter selection remains trial-and-error and expertise-dependent, and that the rationale behind recommended settings in standards (e.g., ASTM E1508, ISO 22309) and vendor guides is sparsely documented or hard to access. Give specific numbers with citations.
